source.title: Extracting Finite Automata from RNNs Using State Merging

record.tranche_reason: The paper mentions grokking speculatively but does not test delayed generalization. Its experiments concern how continued RNN training affects DFA extraction and extracted-state counts.
record.gate_note: The paper reports extraction fidelity, sample efficiency for extracting automata, and changes in extracted DFA size after continued training. Those are not measurements of a grokking test-accuracy delay, the circuit specified in V2, or the other claim versions. Its grokking discussion is speculative and refers to prior work.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a state-merging DFA extraction method for RNNs on Tomita languages. Its RNNs reach 100% generalization accuracy within one or two epochs, so there is no delayed generalization to measure. Continued training changes the extracted DFA size and the extraction sample efficiency, not test accuracy. Grokking is mentioned only speculatively in §5.5, with a citation to Power et al. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that training past convergence improves the sample efficiency of DFA extraction, through an implicit merging or compression of the RNN state space. They call any link to grokking speculative and leave it to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies RNN training on formal-language recognition and DFA extraction; it does not attempt the grokking training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of extraction examples affects extraction performance. The paper also reports differences between checkpoints after 2 and 20 epochs for Tomita 6.

fits_no_version.finding: After the RNN reaches 100% dev accuracy, continued training lowers the number of extraction examples needed to recover the correct DFA (Tomita 6, epoch 2 vs 20). The appendix reports similar behaviour across all languages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training past convergence compresses an RNN's state representations, making automaton extraction more sample-efficient.

fits_no_version.finding: The unminimized extracted DFA size tends to fall gradually with continued training, with spikes. The minimized DFA reaches the true minimum for Tomita 1–6; for Tomita 7 it does so only 3/5 times.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-convergence training performs implicit state merging in RNNs.

record.problems: The grokking connection is speculative and is not tested. The relevant extraction-versus-training results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text; the Tomita 7 result is not reliable.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant rows were included. Other reported extraction-faithfulness and baseline results do not measure any claim version.

untested.parts: All of it: no delayed test-accuracy jump (the RNNs generalize within 1–2 epochs) and no variation of training-set size.
All of it: no generalizing or memorizing circuit is identified, and no progress measure anticipates a generalization jump.
All of it: no grokking on non-algorithmic data and no manipulation of initialization scale.
All of it: no weight-decay manipulation, critical dataset size or ungrokking. Norm growth is mentioned only as a speculative explanation.
All of it: no comparison of algorithms across runs or architectures.
All of it: no optimizer or precision controls.

record.verdict_notes: Post-convergence training that changes the internal representation while accuracy stays at 100% is loosely reminiscent of V2's continuous hidden progress. However, there is no delayed generalization jump to anticipate, so it cannot bear on V2. The training uses AdamW with default hyperparameters, and weight decay is not varied.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test whether test accuracy rises from chance to near-perfect long after training accuracy saturates, or whether that delay depends on training-set size.
It does not identify a generalizing circuit or memorizing components, nor test whether continuous progress measures anticipate a delayed generalization jump.
It does not test grokking on non-algorithmic data or vary initialization scale or weight norm to switch delayed generalization on or off.
It does not study LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
It does not test whether low norm favors an efficient generalizing circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
It does not compare identifiable algorithms learned across runs.
It does not test optimizer or numerical artifacts as an explanation for grokking.

rows.subject: RNN trained on Tomita 6
rows.operation_detail: Compare automaton extraction using representations from RNN checkpoints after 2 and 20 training epochs.
rows.measure: Extracted DFA accuracy against the RNN on the development set, as extraction data varies
rows.note: The text says both checkpoints have 100% RNN development accuracy, while the longer-trained checkpoint yields higher extraction accuracy with fewer extraction examples.
rows.check: The measure is the extracted DFA's accuracy at matching the RNN, not the RNN's test accuracy. The RNN is at 100% dev accuracy at both checkpoints, so this cannot show a grokking delay. The state 'observed' only describes the paper's own extraction finding.

rows.subject: RNNs trained on Tomita 1–6 (reported collectively)
rows.operation_detail: Track the state count of the DFA produced by state merging across training epochs.
rows.measure: Number of states in the DFA before minimization
rows.note: The text describes the state count as generally decreasing gradually with additional training, with some rapid upward spikes.
rows.check: Extracted DFA state count is a property of the extraction method, not a grokking measure, so no version state applies.

rows.subject: RNNs trained on Tomita 1–6 (reported collectively)
rows.operation_detail: Track the state count of the minimized DFA across training epochs.
rows.measure: Number of states in the minimized DFA
rows.note: The text says enough additional training brings the minimized DFA size down to the ideal minimum for Tomita 1–6.
rows.check: Minimized DFA size is not a grokking measure, so no version state applies.

rows.subject: RNNs trained on Tomita 7 (reported collectively)
rows.operation_detail: Track the size and correctness of the minimized DFA across training epochs.
rows.measure: Whether the minimized DFA reaches the true minimum DFA size
rows.note: The text reports that the minimum is not reliably reached for Tomita 7.
rows.check: Not a grokking measure. The value 'correct minimum DFA 3/5 times' comes from the Figure 6 caption (also stated for Table 2), so it is stated in text, not figure-only.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
